assumptions.note: A57 on pointer-chasing engine code; SPEC CPU2006 int on A57-class cores ~1.0-1.2, games lower. Replaced by benchmark B1 (PERF.md 9) on hardware.

cores 0-2 for the application; core 3 is the system's, usable with the core3=1 opt-in (S5 33c0b1b).
work moved off the main thread runs this much as fast on a worker core (cold caches, hand-off waits, migration inside the 0b110 mask).
per-frame hand-offs: ~20 events, the AI spin lock 0x011f11a0, stage semaphores (PERF.md 6.1); B3 measures it.
worst frame / mean frame for 'stable' targets (cell streaming, AI bursts, Havok contacts). 45 fps stable means the worst frame fits 22.2 ms.

lever havok_workers: with iNumHWThreads > 1 the step already runs on AI linear thread 1 (PERF.md 6.11); the MT simulation (iSimType=4, linked natively, 6.9) spreads it over the pool, which relieves that thread's core, not main: no main lever (P0 mtmodel's per-core schedule shows the effect)
lever core3: S5 33c0b1b, off by default; the system's own use of core 3 is unmeasured

lever barrier_relax: in the build: S12 52cb478 ORDER_REFCOUNT=weak is compile.sh's default (ORDERING.md Refcounts; sample 110 increments relaxed, 220 decrements release, 201 sites full); race-checked by mtqemu litmus-order ref; B9 on an A57 confirms the stall saving

lever havok_mt: linked natively (PERF.md 6.9); iSimType=4 selects it (FUN_00c661d0); the step must stay on one thread (CreateObjects keys the pool on the stepping thread id, 6.10); off until mtqemu past WinMain
